### CVE-2026-0106
- Assigner: Google_Devices | Published: 2026-02-05 | Updated: 2026-02-26 | Max CVSS: 9.3
- CWE: Elevation of privilege; CWE-787 CWE-787 Out-of-bounds Write; CWE-125 CWE-125 Out-of-bounds Read; CWE-119 CWE-119 Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 9.3 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

In vpu_mmap of vpu_ioctl, there is a possible arbitrary address mmap due to a missing bounds check. This could lead to local escalation of privilege with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

Affected:
- Google / Android: affected Android kernel

References:
- https://source.android.com/docs/security/bulletin/pixel/2026/2026-02-01 [vendor-advisory]

### CVE-2026-0994 — Denial of Service in Python Protobuf
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-01-23 | Updated: 2026-09-01 | Max CVSS: 8.2
- CWE: CWE-674 CWE-674: Uncontrolled Recursion; CWE-674 Uncontrolled Recursion
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.2 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:L`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial
- CVSS 3.1 (redhat-SADP): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

A denial-of-service (DoS) vulnerability exists in google.protobuf.json_format.ParseDict() in Python, where the max_recursion_depth limit can be bypassed when parsing nested google.protobuf.Any messages.

Due to missing recursion depth accounting inside the internal Any-handling logic, an attacker can supply deeply nested Any structures that bypass the intended recursion limit, eventually exhausting Python’s recursion stack and causing a RecursionError.

Affected:
- Python / Protobuf: affected <=v33.4 (custom)
- Red Hat / Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform 2.5 for RHEL 8: unaffected 0:5.29.6-1.el8ap <* (rpm)

### CVE-2026-1727 — Information Disclosure via Bucket Squatting in Google Cloud Agentspace.
- Assigner: GoogleCloud | Published: 2026-02-06 | Updated: 2026-02-09 | Max CVSS: 9.1
- CWE: CWE-200 CWE-200 Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.1 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:L/SI:L/SA:L/U:Clear`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

The Agentspace service was affected by a vulnerability that exposed sensitive information due to the use of predictable Google Cloud Storage bucket names. These names were utilized for error logs and temporary staging during data imports from GCS and Cloud SQL. This predictability allowed an attacker to engage in "bucket squatting" by establishing these buckets before a victim's initial use.

All versions after December 12th, 2025 have been updated to protect from this vulnerability. No user action is required for this.

Affected:
- Google Cloud / Gemini Enterprise (formerly Agentspace): affected 0 <12/12/2025 (date)

Credits: Omer Amiad

References:
- https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes#February_06_2026

### CVE-2026-1837 — libjxl: Out-of-bounds write in grayscale color transformation when using LCMS2
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-02-11 | Updated: 2026-07-15 | Max CVSS: 8.8
- CWE: CWE-805 CWE-805; CWE-787 Out-of-bounds Write
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.7 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:P/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- CVSS 3.1 (redhat-SADP): 8.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`

A specially-crafted file can cause libjxl's decoder to write pixel data to uninitialized unallocated memory. Soon after that data from another uninitialized unallocated region is copied to pixel data.

This can be done by requesting color transformation of grayscale images to another grayscale color space. Buffers allocated for 1-float-per-pixel are used as if they are allocated for 3-float-per-pixel. That happens only if LCMS2 is used as CMS engine. There is another CMS engine available (selected by build flags).

Affected:
- Google / libjxl: affected 0.9 <=0.11.1 (semver)
- Red Hat / Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10:

  *  for 1.16, upgrade to 1.16.1

### CVE-2026-2472 — Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in Vertex AI Python SDK Visualization
- Assigner: GoogleCloud | Published: 2026-02-20 | Updated: 2026-07-15 | Max CVSS: 8.6
- CWE: CWE-79 CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (XSS or 'Cross-site Scripting'); CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.6 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:P/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:L/SI:L/SA:L/U:Amber`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- CVSS 3.1 (redhat-SADP): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`

Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in the _genai/_evals_visualization component of Google Cloud Vertex AI SDK (google-cloud-aiplatform) versions from 1.98.0 up to (but not including) 1.131.0 allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript in a victim's Jupyter or Colab environment via injecting script escape sequences into model evaluation results or dataset JSON data.

**solutions:** Customers will need to update their google-cloud-aiplatform Python SDK to version 1.131.0 (released on 2025-12-16) or later to receive the fix.

Affected:

### CVE-2026-2473 — Bucket Squatting in Vertex AI Experiments leads to RCE and Model Theft.

- CWE: CWE-340 CWE-340 Generation of Predictable Numbers or Identifiers
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 7.7 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:P/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/U:Clear`

Predictable bucket naming in Vertex AI Experiments in Google Cloud Vertex AI from version 1.21.0 up to (but not including) 1.133.0 on Google Cloud Platform allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to achieve cross-tenant remote code execution, model theft, and poisoning via pre-creating predictably named Cloud Storage buckets (Bucket Squatting).

This vulnerability was patched and no customer action is needed.

Affected:
- Google Cloud / Vertex AI Experiments: affected 1.21.0 <1.133.0 (custom)

Credits: Omer Amiad

### CVE-2026-4810 — Remote Code Execution in Google Agent Development Kit (ADK)
- Assigner: GoogleCloud | Published: 2026-04-13 | Updated: 2026-04-13 | Max CVSS: 9.3
- CWE: CWE-306 CWE-306 Missing authentication for critical function
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.3 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:H/SI:H/SA:H/E:P/U:Amber`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

A Code Injection and Missing Authentication vulnerability in Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) versions 1.7.0 (and 2.0.0a1) through 1.28.1 (and 2.0.0a2) on Python (OSS), Cloud Run, and GKE allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code on the server hosting the ADK instance.

This vulnerability was patched in versions 1.28.1 and 2.0.0a2.


Customers need to redeploy the upgraded ADK to their production environments. In addition, if they are running ADK Web locally, they also need to upgrade their local instance.

**solutions:** Customers need to redeploy the ADK to version 1.28.1 (or 2.0.0a2) or later to receive the fix on their production environments. In addition, if they are running ADK Web locally, they also need to upgrade their local instance.

Affected:
- Google Cloud / Agent Development Kit (ADK): affected 1.7.0 <1.28.1 (custom); affected 2.0.0a1 <2.0.0a2 (custom)

Credits: Yoshizawa

References:

- Assigner: VulDB | Published: 2026-04-03 | Updated: 2026-04-03 | Max CVSS: 6.5

- CVSS 3.0 (cna): 6.3 MEDIUM `CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L/E:P/RL:X/RC:R`
- CVSS 2.0 (cna): 6.5 None `AV:N/AC:L/Au:S/C:P/I:P/A:P/E:POC/RL:ND/RC:UR`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

A security vulnerability has been detected in mixelpixx Google-Research-MCP 1e062d7bd887bfe5f6e582b6cc288bb897b35cf2/ca613b736ab787bc926932f59cddc69457185a83. This issue affects the function extractContent of the file src/services/content-extractor.service.ts of the component Model Context Protocol Handler. The manipulation of the argument URL leads to server-side request forgery. The attack may be initiated remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. This product uses a rolling release model to deliver continuous updates. As a result, specific version information for affected or updated releases is not available. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

Affected:
- mixelpixx / Google-Research-MCP: affected 1e062d7bd887bfe5f6e582b6cc288bb897b35cf2; affected ca613b736ab787bc926932f59cddc69457185a83

### CVE-2026-7428 — Insecure default administrative credentials in AlloyDB for PostgreSQL
- Assigner: GoogleCloud | Published: 2026-05-12 | Updated: 2026-05-12 | Max CVSS: 9.2
- CWE: CWE-1392 CWE-1392 Use of default credentials
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.2 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:L/SI:L/SA:L/U:Amber`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Prior to 2025-11-03, well-intended users of Terraform or REST API for Google Cloud AlloyDB for PostgreSQL could have created clusters with an insecure default password which could have been exploited by a remote attacker to gain full administrative access to the database.




Exploitation required network access to the AlloyDB cluster and was limited to Terraform or the REST API, as other clients blocked it.

**solutions:** This vulnerability was patched on November 3, 2025.



Impacted instances have been proactively remediated, and no customer action is needed.

Affected:
- Google Cloud / AlloyDB for PostgreSQL: affected 0 <2025-11-03 (date)

Credits: Mark Lawrenson

References:
- https://docs.cloud.google.com/alloydb/docs/release-notes#April_28_2026

- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.4 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:A/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:H/SI:H/SA:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

The Model Context Protocol has a security warning advising servers to validate the "Origin" header on all incoming connections to prevent DNS rebinding attacks. Prior to the v0.25.0 release, users had no way to validate the origin's host. In v0.25.0, a new "--allowed-hosts" flag was introduced alongside the existing "--allowed-origins" flag, enabling users to specify permitted hosts at server startup. Both flags default to "*", allowing users to implement strict access controls as needed without breaking existing setups. If either flag is set to "*", the server will output a startup warning about potential vulnerabilities. Documentation has also been updated to highlight these security considerations.

Affected:
- Google / MCP Toolbox for Databases: affected 0 <0.25.0 (semver)

Credits: Jonathan Leitschuh (https://github.com/JLLeitschuh)

References:
- https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox/issues/3113
- https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox/pull/2254

### CVE-2026-11717
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-06-18 | Updated: 2026-06-18 | Max CVSS: 9.3
- CWE: CWE-287 CWE-287: Improper Authentication
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.3 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

An authentication bypass vulnerability exists in the generic opaque token validation path (validateOpaqueToken) of googleapis/mcp-toolbox.

When verifying an unparsed opaque token via an OAuth 2.0 introspection endpoint (RFC 7662), the toolbox decodes the response into an introspectResp struct where the Active field is declared as a pointer to a boolean (*bool). The code only explicitly rejects a token if the response contains a populated active field set to false (if introspectResp.Active != nil && !*introspectResp.Active). If an introspection endpoint responds with a payload that completely omits the mandatory active key, the internal variable remains nil, causing the conditional check to short-circuit. As a result, Toolbox accepts authorization tokens missing the "active" field, granting access to protected tools and underlying data sources.

Affected:
- Google / MCP Toolbox for Databases (googleapis/mcp-toolbox): affected 1.0.0 <=1.3.0 (semver)

Credits: HaoNH Leader Redteam From VINCSS ( Member Of Vingroup )

References:
- https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox/pull/3341

### CVE-2026-11718
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-06-18 | Updated: 2026-06-18 | Max CVSS: 9.3
- CWE: CWE-287 CWE-287: Improper Authentication
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.3 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

An authentication bypass vulnerability exists in the generic opaque token validation path (validateOpaqueToken) of googleapis/mcp-toolbox.

When the toolbox validates an opaque token via an OAuth 2.0 introspection endpoint (RFC 7662), it decodes the response into an introspectResp struct. However, the subsequent claim-checking logic (validateClaims) evaluates the issuer condition as if a.issuer != "" && iss != "". If the external OAuth provider's introspection response omits the optional iss (issuer) field completely, the variable iss defaults to an empty string. This causes the conditional block to evaluate to false and be skipped silently. Consequently, the application accepts tokens issued by unauthorized or unintended third-party identity providers.

Affected:
- Google / MCP Toolbox for Databases (googleapis/mcp-toolbox): affected 1.0.0 <=1.3.0 (semver)

Credits: HaoNH Leader Redteam From VINCSS ( Member Of Vingroup ).

References:
- https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox/pull/3360

### CVE-2026-11719
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-06-18 | Updated: 2026-06-18 | Max CVSS: 8.6
- CWE: CWE-862 CWE-862: Missing Authorization
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.6 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

An authenticated authorization bypass vulnerability exists in MCP Toolbox for Databases due to missing scope enforcement across older protocol handlers.

While the 2025-11-25 protocol version handler correctly enforces per-tool restrictions defined by scopesRequired, older supported protocol versions (2025-06-18, 2025-03-26, and 2024-11-05) omit this check. An authenticated client with low-privilege tokens (e.g., read) can bypass the intended per-tool scope restrictions and execute high-privilege tools (e.g., admin) simply by specifying an older protocol version in the MCP-Protocol-Version header, or by omitting the header entirely (which causes the server to default to the vulnerable 2024-11-05 handler).

Affected:
- Google / MCP Toolbox for Databases (googleapis/mcp-toolbox): affected 1.3.0

Credits: HE WEI（ギカク）(https://www.linkedin.com/in/gikaku/)

References:
- https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox/pull/3335
- https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox/pull/3049

### CVE-2026-11720 — Path Traversal in googleapis/mcp-toolbox HTTP Tool URL Builder
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-06-29 | Updated: 2026-06-29 | Max CVSS: 9.3
- CWE: CWE-22 CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.3 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

A path traversal vulnerability exists in the HTTP tool URL builder of googleapis/mcp-toolbox.

When constructing downstream API requests, the URL builder substitutes user-controlled pathParams into the configured tool path and parses the resulting string as a relative URL. While it checks that the input does not alter the scheme, host, or user info, it relies on ResolveReference for the final URL resolution. Because dot segments (../) are normalized during this resolution step, an attacker can supply path parameters containing directory traversal sequences to escape the operator-configured path scope. This allows the client to coerce the toolbox into making requests to unintended endpoints on the same target host while forwarding the toolbox's configured credentials (e.g., bypassing a restricted path like /api/v1/users/{{.id}} to reach /admin/secrets).

Affected:
- Google / MCP Toolbox for Databases (googleapis/mcp-toolbox): affected 0 <1.3.0 (semver)

Credits: Ryan Vonbrubeck / @dodge1218

References:
- https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox/pull/3218

### CVE-2026-11998 — AngularJS XSS via SCE resource URL sanitization bypass
- Assigner: HeroDevs | Published: 2026-06-24 | Updated: 2026-08-05 | Max CVSS: 7.6
- CWE: CWE-791 CWE-791 Incomplete filtering of special elements; CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.6 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:L`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial
- CVSS 3.1 (redhat-SADP): 7.6 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:L`

A flaw in AngularJS' Strict Contextual Escaping (SCE) logic allows bypassing certain SCE policies for resource URLs and can lead to arbitrary JavaScript execution within the context of the victim's browser session.


SCE's purpose is to ensure that only trusted or safe values are used in certain security-sensitive contexts, such as resource URLs, including URLs that define executable JavaScript scripts, '<iframe>' documents, route templates, etc. A flaw in the logic that tries to match entire URLs against regular expression matchers can result in partial matches for certain types of regular expressions, effectively bypassing the policies and allowing the use of unsafe values as resource URLs.


This issue affects AngularJS versions greater than or equal to 1.2.0-rc.3.


Note:
The AngularJS project was already End-of-Life when this CVE was published and will not receive any updates to address this issue. For more information see the  End-of-Life announcement https://docs.angularjs.org/misc/version-support-status .

### CVE-2026-12537 — Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in Gemini CLI CI/CD Workflows
- Assigner: GoogleCloud | Published: 2026-06-24 | Updated: 2026-06-24 | Max CVSS: 10
- CWE: CWE-20 CWE-20 Improper Input Validation
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 10 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:H/SI:H/SA:H/U:Clear`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

Improper Neutralization used in an OS Command in the container launcher in Google Gemini CLI (versions prior to 0.39.1) and run-gemini-cli GitHub Action (versions prior to 0.1.22) on headless CI platforms allows an unprivileged attacker to achieve pre-sandbox host-level code execution a maliciously crafted .gemini/.env file.

**solutions:** Ensure you are using the latest version of gemini cli and follow the  best practices guide https://github.com/google-github-actions/run-gemini-cli/blob/main/docs/trust-guidance.md .

Affected:
- Google Cloud / Gemini CLI: affected 0 <0.39.1 (custom)
- Google Cloud / run-gemini-cli GitHub Action: affected 0 <0.1.22 (custom)

Credits: Elad Meged of Novee Security; Devansh Batham

References:
- https://github.com/google-github-actions/run-gemini-cli/security/advisories/GHSA-wpqr-6v78-jr5g

### CVE-2026-12681
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-06-24 | Updated: 2026-06-24 | Max CVSS: 8.9
- CWE: CWE-1285 CWE-1285 Improper validation of specified index, position, or offset in input
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.9 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:H/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

Improper Validation of Specified Index, Position, or Offset in Input vulnerability in Google go-attestation. parseEfiSignatureList() does not advance the buffer past vendor bytes before reading entries. For hashSHA256SigGUID lists, this allows attacker-controlled vendor header bytes to be appended to the trusted SHA256 hash list. A crafted TPM event log could inject arbitrary SHA256 hashes into the verifier's trusted measurement database, enabling a remote attestation verifier to accept a compromised boot state. This issue affects go-attestation: through 0.6.0.

Affected:
- Google / go-attestation: affected 0 <=0.6.0 (semver)

Credits: https://github.com/prasanna8585

References:
- https://github.com/google/go-attestation/security/advisories/GHSA-9r4w-jg96-92mv

### CVE-2026-12710 — Missing Authorization in Application Integration QueryEngineTask
- Assigner: GoogleCloud | Published: 2026-08-22 | Updated: 2026-08-26 | Max CVSS: 9.3
- CWE: CWE-862 CWE-862 Missing Authorization
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.3 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/U:Clear`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

A Missing Authorization vulnerability in the QueryEngineTask of Google Cloud Application Integration (versions from 2025-04-28 to 2026-04-04) allows an external attacker to access sensitive internal data.




The issue was patched on April 4, 2026; no customer action is required.

**solutions:** Access is now restricted and the issue is resolved.


Integrations using QueryEngineTask for external traffic will return a PERMISSION_DENIED error. We recommend that customers remove or replace any QueryEngineTask (ASIS_TEMPLATE) tasks in their Application Integration workflows.

Affected:
- Google Cloud / Application Integration: affected 2025-04-28 <2026-04-04 (date)

Credits: Guillaume Berleur

References:
- https://cloud.google.com/application-integration/docs/release-notes#August_21_2026

### CVE-2026-12715 — Missing Authorization in Firebase Studio allows Cross-Tenant Source Code Theft
- Assigner: GoogleCloud | Published: 2026-07-17 | Updated: 2026-07-17 | Max CVSS: 8.5
- CWE: CWE-862 CWE-862 Missing Authorization
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.5 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:H/SI:H/SA:H/U:Clear`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

Missing Authorization in Google Cloud Firebase Studio versions prior to 2026-04-15 on Google Cloud Platform allows an attacker to download other users' deployed source code and access sensitive data via unauthorized GCS URL signing requests.


This vulnerability was patched on 15 April 2026, and no customer action is needed.

**solutions:** This vulnerability was patched on April 15, 2026 on the server-side.

As a precautionary measure, users who may have stored sensitive information such as API keys (e.g., GEMINI_API_KEY) within their Firebase Studio workspace may choose to rotate these keys.

Instructions for rotating the GEMINI_API_KEY can be found at  https://firebase.google.com/docs/studio/troubleshooting#rotate-gemini-key .

Affected:
- Google Cloud / Firebase Studio: affected 0 <2026-04-15 (date)

Credits: A Security Researcher

References:
- https://docs.cloud.google.com/support/bulletins#gcp-2026-043

### CVE-2026-13745 — Arbitrary Code Execution in Gemini CLI via Untrusted Local .env Files Overriding GEMINI_CLI_HOME
- Assigner: GoogleCloud | Published: 2026-09-10 | Updated: 2026-09-23 | Max CVSS: 7.7
- CWE: CWE-829 CWE-829 Inclusion of functionality from untrusted control sphere; CWE-15 CWE-15 External Control of System or Configuration Setting
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 7.7 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:P/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/U:Amber`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

A vulnerability in the Gemini CLI prior to version 0.39.1 allows attackers to achieve arbitrary code execution by tricking a victim into starting the CLI within an untrusted directory. The vulnerability is triggered via untrusted .env files overriding GEMINI_CLI_HOME to load malicious configuration files and bypass folder trust prompts.

**solutions:** *  Upgrade: Ensure you are using the latest version of gemini cli and follow the best practices guide https://github.com/google-github-actions/run-gemini-cli/blob/main/docs/trust-guidance.md
  *  Configure Trust: Determine if your CI workflow operates on trusted or untrusted data. If the data is fully trusted, set GEMINI_TRUST_WORKSPACE: 'true' in your workflow.

Affected:
- Google Cloud / Gemini CLI: affected 0 <0.39.1 (custom)

Credits: Benjamin Faller, Redguard AG

References:
- https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/releases/tag/v0.39.1
- https://www.redguard.ch/blog/2026/06/03/advisory-google-gemini-cli/
- https://www.pwned.info/articles/homing-in-on-arbitrary-code-execution-within-gemini-cli/

### CVE-2026-14204 — Google Authenticator < 0.56 - 2FA Secret Overwrite via CSRF
- Assigner: WPScan | Published: 2026-08-06 | Updated: 2026-08-06 | Max CVSS: 6.5
- CWE: CWE-352 Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF); CWE-352 CWE-352 Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 6.5 MEDIUM `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

The Google Authenticator WordPress plugin before 0.56 does not verify a CSRF nonce when saving its two-factor setup, allowing attackers to trick a logged-in user into overwriting their own 2FA secret with an attacker-controlled value, which enables two-factor authentication and locks the victim out of their account.

Affected:
- Unknown / Google Authenticator: affected 0 <0.56 (semver)

Credits: Miguel Mendez Z; WPScan

References:
- https://wpscan.com/vulnerability/9ae793b2-31d4-4a9d-9481-52f07024b07e/ [exploit,vdb-entry,technical-description]

### CVE-2026-14537 — Authorization Bypass in MCP Toolbox Legacy HTTP Endpoints
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-07-31 | Updated: 2026-07-31 | Max CVSS: 8.1
- CWE: CWE-863 CWE-863 (Incorrect Authorization)
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/E:U`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

Incorrect Authorization in the direct HTTP API tool invocation endpoint in Google mcp-toolbox versions v1.3.0 and v1.4.0 allows an unauthenticated attacker to invoke tools protected by the scopeRequired feature via sending tool invocation requests through legacy HTTP endpoints when the --enable-api flag is active.

Affected:
- Google / mcp-toolbox: affected 1.3.0; affected v1.4.0

Credits: HE WEI (ギカク); David Carliez

References:
- https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox/pull/3435

### CVE-2026-14540 — Server-Side Request Forgery via Unrestricted HTTP Redirection in MCP Toolbox
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-07-31 | Updated: 2026-07-31 | Max CVSS: 8
- CWE: CWE-918 CWE-918 (Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF))
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/E:U`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

A Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability exists in the generic HTTP source and tool components of Google mcp-toolbox versions 0.3.0 through 1.4.0. While the toolbox implements baseline input sanitization for user-controlled parameters, the underlying HTTP client (internal/sources/http/http.go) fails to safely regulate request redirection boundaries. Specifically, the client is initialized without a restrictive CheckRedirect policy hook and lacks target IP validation. An attacker or a malicious data-driven prompt can supply a crafted path parameter that triggers an open redirect or a direct destination swap on the target backend, coercing the mcp-toolbox into blindly following the redirection and making unauthorized requests to internal or arbitrary external endpoints.

Affected:
- Google / mcp-toolbox: affected 0.3.0 <=1.4.0 (semver)

Credits: Syed Anas Mohiuddin

References:
- https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox/pull/3448

### CVE-2026-14541 — Authentication Bypass and Audience Confusion in MCP Toolbox OAuth Provider
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-07-31 | Updated: 2026-07-31 | Max CVSS: 8
- CWE: CWE-287 CWE-287 (Improper Authentication)
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/E:U`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

An authentication bypass and audience confusion vulnerability exists in the Google OAuth provider component of Google mcp-toolbox version 1.4.0. When a Google authService is initialized with mcpEnabled: true but lacks an explicitly defined audience or clientId, the ValidateMCPAuth pipeline for opaque tokens skips audience validation entirely. As a result, the toolbox will accept any valid Google OAuth access token—even those minted for unrelated ecosystem applications—granting unauthorized clients access to protected tools and data backends.

Affected:
- Google / mcp-toolbox: affected 1.4.0 (semver)

Credits: HE WEI (ギカク)

References:
- https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox/pull/3450

- Assigner: GoogleCloud | Published: 2026-07-13 | Updated: 2026-07-13 | Max CVSS: 9.4

- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

A Missing Authorization vulnerability in the repository creation functionality in Google Cloud BigQuery, Dataform and Colab Enterprise, in the versions between October 2025 and May 10th, 2026, on Google Cloud Platform, allows an authenticated attacker to escalate privileges and perform cross-tenant repository takeover.


This vulnerability was patched on 10 May 2026, and no customer action is needed.

- Google Cloud / BigQuery: affected 2025-10 <2026-05-10 (date)
- Google Cloud / Dataform: affected 2025-10 <2026-05-10 (date)
- Google Cloud / Colab Enterprise: affected 2025-10 <2026-05-10 (date)

Credits: Omer Amiad

### CVE-2026-15432 — Observable Timing Discrepancy in Tink-Java and Tink-Android ChunkedMacVerification
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-07-21 | Updated: 2026-07-22 | Max CVSS: 8.2
- CWE: CWE-208 CWE-208 Observable Timing Discrepancy
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.2 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

When verifying a mac with a ChunkedMacVerification object, Tink compares the resulting tag with non constant time comparison. This potentially allows an attacker to use timinig information as a side channel in order to get information how many bytes of a given tag match the correct tag. This in turn could allow to find a correct tag bytewise.

Affected:
- Google / Tink-Java: affected All releases before 1.21.0, including 1.21.0.
- Google / Tink-Android: affected All releases before 1.21.0, including 1.21.0.

References:
- https://github.com/tink-crypto/tink-java/issues/75

### CVE-2026-15810 — Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in Looker allows Admin Account Takeover
- Assigner: GoogleCloud | Published: 2026-07-24 | Updated: 2026-07-24 | Max CVSS: 8.7
- CWE: CWE-79 CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (XSS or 'Cross-site Scripting')
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.7 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:P/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:L/SI:L/SA:L/U:Amber`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

A Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in Google Cloud Looker versions prior to 25.6.103, 25.12.65, 25.18.68, 26.0.66, 26.2.47, 26.4.36, 26.6.28, and 26.8.7 on Looker-hosted and Self-hosted allows an attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript leading to administrative account takeover using a maliciously crafted URL.


Looker-hosted and Self-hosted were found to be vulnerable.
This issue has already been mitigated for Looker-hosted instances. No user action is required for these.


Self-hosted instances must be upgraded to the patched versions: 25.6.103+, 25.12.65+, 25.18.68+, 26.0.66+, 26.2.47+, 26.4.36+, 26.6.28+, or 26.8.7+.

**solutions:** This vulnerability has been mitigated for Looker-hosted instances, and no user action is required.

For Self-hosted Looker instances, customers should upgrade to one of the patched versions or later: 25.6.103+, 25.12.65+, 25.18.68+, 26.0.66+, 26.2.47+, 26.4.36+, 26.6.28+, or 26.8.7+.

Affected:
- Google Cloud / Looker: affected 0 <25.6.103 (custom); affected 0 <25.12.65 (custom); affected 0 <25.18.68 (custom); affected 0 <26.0.66 (custom); affected 0 <26.2.47 (custom); affected 0 <26.4.36 (custom); affected 0 <26.6.28 (custom); affected 0 <26.8.7 (custom)
- Google Cloud / Looker: affected 0 <25.6.103 (custom); affected 0 <25.12.65 (custom); affected 0 <25.18.68 (custom); affected 0 <26.0.66 (custom); affected 0 <26.2.47 (custom); affected 0 <26.4.36 (custom); affected 0 <26.6.28 (custom); affected 0 <26.8.7 (custom)

Credits: Sivanesh Ashok; Sreeram KL

- https://docs.cloud.google.com/looker/docs/release-notes#July_22_2026

### CVE-2026-15829 — SQL Injection and Security Boundary Bypass in googleapis/mcp-toolbox
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-07-21 | Updated: 2026-07-22 | Max CVSS: 8.6
- CWE: CWE-89 CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection'); CWE-863 CWE-863: Incorrect Authorization
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.6 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

A SQL injection (CWE-89) and security boundary bypass (CWE-863) vulnerability exists in the prebuilt BigQuery forecasting tool (bigquery-forecast) of googleapis/mcp-toolbox.

The tool accepts client-controlled parameters (data_col, timestamp_col, and id_cols) as plain strings and interpolates them unescaped via fmt.Sprintf directly into a generated AI.FORECAST table-valued SELECT statement. While MCP Toolbox utilizes an allowedDatasets mechanism to restrict queries, this defense only validates the history_data parameter; the final assembled query is executed without re-validation.

An attacker can break out of the string literal fields (such as timestamp_col) to inject a valid multi-statement or cross-dataset query block. This allows an unauthorized user to bypass the operator-configured allowedDatasets boundary and read arbitrary BigQuery tables.

Affected:
- Google / MCP Toolbox for Databases (googleapis/mcp-toolbox): affected 0.13.0 <=1.3.0 (semver)

Credits: Matteo Panzeri (Università di Pavia), GitHub @matte1782

References:
- https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox/pull/3324

### CVE-2026-18236 — Google-ADK Continuation Forgery
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-07-29 | Updated: 2026-07-29 | Max CVSS: 9.3
- CWE: CWE-863 CWE-863 Incorrect Authorization
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.3 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:H/SI:H/SA:H/E:P`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

A vulnerability in the Agent Development Kit (ADK) allows for continuation forgery in tool confirmations. An attacker who is able to manipulate or inject events into the session history can execute unauthorized tools by forging a tool confirmation response. This is possible because the framework did not verify if the target tool was registered to the executing agent, did not validate if the tool actually required confirmation, and did not match the confirmation arguments against the original tool call event in the history.

Affected:
- Google / Google-ADK: affected < 2.5.0

Credits: Aviyam Ivgi

References:
- https://github.com/google/adk-python/commit/c03f333769feaeaa9fe8910fbe95cb9f2d513f54

### CVE-2026-19202 — Token Cache Reuse in mcp-toolbox-sdk-python
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-09-22 | Updated: 2026-09-23 | Max CVSS: 9.1
- CWE: CWE-524 CWE-524: Use of a Shared Cache with Insufficient Key Granularity
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.1 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

A caching flaw in the toolbox-core package of the mcp-toolbox-sdk-python SDK causes the same Google ID token to be cached and reused across different audiences. If an application uses the SDK to authenticate to two or more different audiences within the same process, the module-level token cache fails to key its cached tokens by the requested audience. Consequently, a valid, unexpired token minted for a sensitive service (Service A) can be retrieved from the cache and sent to a secondary service (Service B). An attacker who operates, compromises, or monitors traffic to Service B can capture this token and replay it to impersonate the victim application against Service A.

Affected:
- Google / mcp-toolbox-sdk-python: affected 0 <=1.1.0 (custom)

Credits: HE WEI（ギカク)

References:
- https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox-sdk-python/pull/675 [patch]

**solutions:** Users of the google-cloud-aiplatform SDK should upgrade to version 1.165.1 or later, or ensure that an explicit staging_bucket belonging to their project is specified when calling Model.upload().

### CVE-2026-66901 — Google::Auth versions before 0.09 for Perl allow server side request forgery and credential exfiltration via unvalidated URLs taken from the credentials JSON
- Assigner: CPANSec | Published: 2026-08-04 | Updated: 2026-08-05 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-918 CWE-918 Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF); CWE-201 CWE-201 Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Google::Auth versions before 0.09 for Perl allow server side request forgery and credential exfiltration via unvalidated URLs taken from the credentials JSON.

The URLs the library requests are read from the credentials JSON, and their hosts were not checked against the universe domain before the request. For an external_account configuration, retrieve_subject_token fetched credential_source.url with headers from the same JSON, and fetch_access_token posted the subject token to token_url, then sent the STS access token it received to service_account_impersonation_url in an Authorization: Bearer header. The authorized_user, impersonated_service_account and service_account configurations posted the client secret and refresh token, the source access token, and a signed JWT assertion to their own JSON-supplied token_uri or impersonation URL.

Any caller that builds credentials from a configuration it does not fully control issues those requests from the application's network position, reaching hosts the configuration names, including internal services and link-local metadata endpoints, and hands them the credentials each request carries. The service_account assertion is bound to aud, so it is not replayable against Google.

Version 0.06 added a _validate_url host check to the external_account class, keyed on a universe_domain read from the same credentials JSON. Version 0.07 gated a JSON-supplied universe domain behind GOOGLE_EXTERNAL_ACCOUNT_ALLOW_CUSTOM_UNIVERSES=1, deriving the pin flag from arguments that an earlier BUILDARGS pass had already merged on the make_creds path. Version 0.08 passed the pin decision through as an explicit constructor argument and moved _validate_url to Google::Auth::Credentials, adding the call to UserRefreshCredentials and ImpersonatedServiceAccountCredentials, and 0.09 added it to ServiceAccountCredentials.

**workarounds:** For deployments that cannot upgrade to 0.09, ensure that every credentials configuration reaching the Application Default Credentials flow comes from a trusted source.

**solutions:** Upgrade to Google-Auth 0.09 or later, which validates each URL host against googleapis.com or a universe domain pinned by the application before the request.

Affected:
- CJCOLLIER / Google::Auth: affected 0 <0.09 (custom) files: lib/Google/Auth/ExternalAccountCredentials.pm, lib/Google/Auth/ServiceAccountCredentials.pm, lib/Google/Auth/UserRefreshCredentials.pm, lib/Google/Auth/ImpersonatedServiceAccountCredentials.pm

References:
- https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/google-auth-library-perl/commit/c95c77e70bec94f17e239d88050f843ea1cade95.patch [patch]
- https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/google-auth-library-perl/commit/cd42bdef53afcc4531161e85e91d0d5997e01324.patch [patch]
- https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/google-auth-library-perl/commit/9b5157062acc605ca9e6c507b910587f4829ce9e.patch [patch]
- https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/google-auth-library-perl/commit/cbbb07804e3f8cc7cf9638ecc9c2097d80a9ef50.patch [patch]
- https://metacpan.org/release/CJCOLLIER/Google-Auth-0.09/changes [release-notes]

### CVE-2026-66902 — Google::Auth versions before 0.06 for Perl run a command named in an external_account credentials JSON via an ungated system call
- Assigner: CPANSec | Published: 2026-08-04 | Updated: 2026-08-05 | Max CVSS: 9.8
- CWE: CWE-78 CWE-78 Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection'); CWE-829 CWE-829 Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 9.8 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

Google::Auth versions before 0.06 for Perl run a command named in an external_account credentials JSON via an ungated system call.

The Pluggable subclass reads credential_source.executable.command from the credentials JSON and runs it as `system($command)`, a single argument call that passes the whole string to /bin/sh -c. The executable's environment_variables map from the same JSON is copied into %ENV first. No opt-in gate guards the call. make_creds selects the Pluggable subclass whenever credential_source.executable is present, so the path is reached from the standard Application Default Credentials flow, including a "type": "external_account" configuration read from the file named by GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS. Configurations without credential_source.executable do not select this subclass and do not reach the call.

Any caller that builds credentials from a configuration it does not fully control runs the embedded command with the privileges of the application process.

**workarounds:** For deployments that cannot upgrade to 0.06, apply the upstream fix commit, or ensure that every credentials configuration reaching the Application Default Credentials flow comes from a trusted source.

**solutions:** Upgrade to Google-Auth 0.06 or later, which throws unless the environment variable GOOGLE_EXTERNAL_ACCOUNT_ALLOW_EXECUTABLES is set to 1.

Affected:
- CJCOLLIER / Google::Auth: affected 0 <0.06 (custom) files: lib/Google/Auth/ExternalAccountCredentials/Pluggable.pm

References:
- https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/google-auth-library-perl/commit/c95c77e70bec94f17e239d88050f843ea1cade95.patch [patch]
- https://metacpan.org/release/CJCOLLIER/Google-Auth-0.06/diff/CJCOLLIER/Google-Auth-0.05
- http://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/08/04/35

### CVE-2026-74759 — Google::Auth versions 0.12 for Perl allow server side request forgery via unvalidated credential_source URLs in AWS external account credentials
- Assigner: CPANSec | Published: 2026-11-01 | Updated: 2026-11-06 | Max CVSS: 9.8
- CWE: CWE-918 CWE-918 Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 9.8 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

Google::Auth versions 0.12 for Perl allow server side request forgery via unvalidated credential_source URLs in AWS external account credentials.

An external_account configuration with the AWS subject token type selects Google::Auth::ExternalAccountCredentials::Aws. Its retrieve_subject_token sends requests to the imdsv2_session_token_url, url and region_url fields of credential_source without the host check that the other credential classes apply.

Any caller that builds credentials from a configuration it does not fully control issues GET and PUT requests to hosts the configuration names, including internal services and link-local metadata endpoints.

**workarounds:** Ensure that every credentials configuration reaching the Application Default Credentials flow comes from a trusted source.

**solutions:** Upgrade to a future Google-Auth release.

Affected:
-  / Google-Auth: affected 0.12 (custom) files: lib/Google/Auth/ExternalAccountCredentials/Aws.pm

References:
- https://metacpan.org/release/CJCOLLIER/Google-Auth-0.12/source/lib/Google/Auth/ExternalAccountCredentials/Aws.pm [technical-description]

- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Google::Auth versions from 0.11 through 0.12 for Perl accept an authorization code from any local process because the gcloud-auth login callback does not check the OAuth state.

The gcloud-auth login and application-default login commands send a state parameter with the authorization request, then take the code from the first request to reach their loopback listener without comparing the returned state.

A local attacker can submit an authorization code for their own Google account. The CLI exchanges it and stores the refresh token as the user's credentials, so the user's tools then act as the attacker's account.

**workarounds:** Run gcloud-auth login and gcloud-auth application-default login with --no-browser, which uses the out-of-band flow without a loopback listener.

**solutions:** Upgrade to a future Google-Auth release.

Affected:
-  / Google-Auth: affected 0.11 <=0.12 (custom) files: bin/gcloud-auth.pl

References:
- https://metacpan.org/release/CJCOLLIER/Google-Auth-0.12/source/bin/gcloud-auth.pl [technical-description]

### CVE-2026-75062 — Eval Injection in google/langfun via default lf.query protocol
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-08-26 | Updated: 2026-08-27 | Max CVSS: 9.2
- CWE: CWE-95 CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection'); CWE-1188 CWE-1188: Insecure Default Initialization of Resource
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.2 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection') in the default lf.query Python protocol in Google langfun versions prior to 0.1.2 allows remote unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary Python code in the context of the host application via crafted prompt inputs that cause the model to generate executable Python expressions evaluated without a sandbox.

Affected:
- Google / langfun: affected 0.0.1 <0.1.2 (semver)

Credits: Hamza Haroon

### CVE-2026-85268 — Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in Firebase Auth Handler via Malicious Bundle ID
- Assigner: GoogleCloud | Published: 2026-10-30 | Updated: 2026-10-30 | Max CVSS: 8.7
- CWE: CWE-79 CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (XSS or 'Cross-site Scripting')
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.7 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:P/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:L/SI:L/SA:L/U:Amber`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

A Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) (CWE-79) vulnerability in the auth/handler in Google Cloud Identity Platform and Firebase Authentication versions prior to 2026-08-14 on iOS allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript using a malicious iOS bundle ID.

**solutions:** This vulnerability has been patched for all users and no app updates are required. Action is only needed for developers who followed Option 4 (self-hosting the helper code) in the Firebase redirect best practices documentation https://firebase.google.com/docs/auth/web/redirect-best-practices#self-host-helper-code. These users should re-synchronize the helper code to make sure they are hosting the latest version.

Affected:
- Google Cloud / Identity Platform and Firebase Authentication: affected 0 <2026-08-14 (date)

Credits: Mathias Karlsson

References:
- https://firebase.google.com/support/releases#auth-helper-fix

### CVE-2026-85520 — Unauthenticated arbitrary file write leading to RCE in gmfeed PrestaShop module
- Assigner: CERT-PL | Published: 2026-09-29 | Updated: 2026-09-29 | Max CVSS: 9.3
- CWE: CWE-73 CWE-73 External control of file name or path
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.3 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:L/SI:L/SA:L`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

Google Merchant Center Feed (gmfeed) module for PrestaShop is vulnerable to unauthenticated arbitrary file write in the feed.php endpoint. An unauthenticated attacker can send a crafted request that controls the output file name, path, extension, and content through request parameters. Due to the lack of authentication and input validation, the request is processed successfully, allowing an attacker to write and execute arbitrary PHP code, resulting in remote code execution (RCE).


This issue was fixed in version 2.3.9.

Affected:
- MyPresta / Google Merchant Center Feed: affected 1.9.1 <=2.3.8 (semver)

Credits: Today Group sp. z o.o.

References:
- https://cert.pl/en/posts/2026/09/CVE-2026-85520 [third-party-advisory]

### CVE-2026-87720 — Incorrect Authorization via Stale ProjectCache Eviction and Repeated .git Suffixes in Gerrit Code Review
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-09-24 | Updated: 2026-09-25 | Max CVSS: 7.6
- CWE: CWE-863 CWE-863 Incorrect Authorization; CWE-613 CWE-613 Insufficient Session Expiration; CWE-706 CWE-706 Use of Incorrectly-Resolved Name or Reference
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 7.6 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Incorrect Authorization (CWE-863) in project name normalization (ProjectUtil.stripGitSuffix) and ProjectCache eviction logic (ProjectCacheImpl) in Gerrit Code Review versions 2.16.0 through 3.12.9, 3.13.0 through 3.13.8, and 3.14.0 through 3.14.2 allows an authenticated user (or an unauthenticated user if the repository was previously public) to cause unauthorized disclosure of private repository content and durable restoration of revoked project-owner administrative privileges via crafted requests using repeated .git suffixes (such as project.git.git) across REST APIs, Gitiles, or SSH Git commands. Because Gerrit strips only a single terminal .git suffix when constructing the logical ProjectCache key while JGit (FileKey.lenient) resolves the suffixed alias to the same canonical bare repository on disk, revoking read access or removing owner rules on the canonical project name fails to evict the cached alias ProjectState during the cache validity window, enabling reads of newly created private commits or writes to refs/meta/config. This issue is fixed in Gerrit Code Review versions 3.12.10, 3.13.9, and 3.14.3.

Affected:
- Gerrit / Gerrit: affected 2.16.0 <3.12.10 (semver); affected 3.13.0 <3.13.9 (semver); affected 3.14.0 <3.14.3 (semver)

Credits: Jaime Cavero

References:
- https://issues.gerritcodereview.com/issues/538883789

### CVE-2026-87721 — Denial of Service via Exponential Backtracking in ANTLR Search Query Parser in Gerrit Code Review
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-09-24 | Updated: 2026-09-25 | Max CVSS: 8.7
- CWE: CWE-400 CWE-400 Uncontrolled Resource Consumption; CWE-407 CWE-407 Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity; CWE-834 CWE-834 Excessive Iteration
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.7 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Uncontrolled Resource Consumption (CWE-400 / CWE-407) in the ANTLR 3 search query parser (QueryParser / Query.g) in Gerrit Code Review versions 2.0.19 through 3.12.9, 3.13.0 through 3.13.8, and 3.14.0 through 3.14.2 allows an unauthenticated remote attacker (or an authenticated user if anonymous read access is disabled) to cause a persistent denial of service (CPU exhaustion and HTTP worker thread pool starvation requiring a server restart) via crafted search queries containing deeply nested parentheses sent to query evaluation endpoints (/changes/?q=, /accounts/?q=, /groups/?query=, /projects/?query=, /Documentation/?q=, /changes/{id}/query?expression=, or SSH gerrit query). Because syntactic predicates in conditionOr and conditionAnd recurse via conditionBase without memoization prior to capability or visibility checks and worker threads do not abort when the client disconnects, a small number of requests (such as 25 requests matching default httpd.maxThreads) can permanently pin all HTTP worker threads. This issue is fixed in Gerrit Code Review versions 3.12.10, 3.13.9, and 3.14.3.

Affected:
- Gerrit / Gerrit: affected 2.0.19 <3.12.10 (semver); affected 3.13.0 <3.13.9 (semver); affected 3.14.0 <3.14.3 (semver)

Credits: Amin Alemi

References:
- https://issues.gerritcodereview.com/issues/541287630

### CVE-2026-87722 — Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) in Search Query Predicates and REST Filter Endpoints in Gerrit Code Review
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-09-24 | Updated: 2026-09-25 | Max CVSS: 8.7
- CWE: CWE-400 CWE-400 Uncontrolled Resource Consumption; CWE-1333 CWE-1333 Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.7 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Uncontrolled Resource Consumption (CWE-400 / CWE-1333) in regex search query predicates (such as RegexProjectPredicate, RegexRefPredicate, RegexPathPredicate, and sibling predicates) and REST regex filter endpoints (RegexListSearcher /projects/?r= and RefFilter /projects/{project}/branches/?r=) in Gerrit Code Review versions 2.1.6 through 3.12.9, 3.13.0 through 3.13.8, and 3.14.0 through 3.14.2 allows an unauthenticated remote attacker (or an authenticated user if anonymous read access is disabled) to cause a denial of service (CPU starvation and JVM heap exhaustion / OutOfMemoryError) via crafted search queries or REST API requests containing regular expressions with large counted repetitions or exponential DFA determinization patterns. Because the user-supplied regular expression is compiled into an unbounded dk.brics.automaton instance (new RegExp(re).toAutomaton()) on the request thread prior to index evaluation or access control visibility filtering, trivial queries can exhaust JVM heap or pin request threads regardless of heap size. This issue is fixed in Gerrit Code Review versions 3.12.10, 3.13.9, and 3.14.3.

Affected:
- Gerrit / Gerrit: affected 2.1.6 <3.12.10 (semver); affected 3.13.0 <3.13.9 (semver); affected 3.14.0 <3.14.3 (semver)

Credits: Amin Alemi

References:
- https://issues.gerritcodereview.com/issues/540877705

### CVE-2026-89418 — Uncontrolled Recursion leading to Denial of Service in protobuf-javascript (google-protobuf)
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-09-17 | Updated: 2026-09-17 | Max CVSS: 8.7
- CWE: CWE-674 CWE-674 Uncontrolled Recursion
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.7 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

google-protobuf contains an unbounded recursion when parsing unknown protobuf group fields. An attacker can send a small crafted payload of deeply nested START_GROUP wire bytes to any Node.js service that calls the generated deserializeBinary() API, causing a RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded and crashing the process. No authentication or prior knowledge of the schema is required.

Affected:
- Google / protobuf-javascript (aka google-protobuf npm package): affected All versions

Credits: EQSTLab&@232-323

References:
- https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf-javascript/security/advisories/GHSA-5h29-r2cp-hfmr

### CVE-2026-93327 — Unsafe Java Deserialization in Application Integration SubWorkflow tasks allows Remote Code Execution
- Assigner: GoogleCloud | Published: 2026-10-30 | Updated: 2026-10-30 | Max CVSS: 9.4
- CWE: CWE-502 CWE-502 Deserialization of Untrusted Data
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.4 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:H/SI:H/SA:H/U:Clear`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

A Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in the SubWorkflow task in Google Cloud Application Integration versions prior to 2026-09-11 on Google Cloud Platform allows an authenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code using a maliciously crafted serialized object.


This vulnerability was patched on 11 September 2026, and no customer action is needed.

- Google Cloud / Application Integration: affected 0 <2026-09-11 (date)

Credits: Saurav Bhattarai

### CVE-2026-93328 — Missing Authorization in MCP Toolbox for Databases allows Arbitrary File Read and Write
- Assigner: GoogleCloud | Published: 2026-10-26 | Updated: 2026-10-26 | Max CVSS: 9.3
- CWE: CWE-862 CWE-862 Missing Authorization; CWE-22 CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.3 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:L/SI:L/SA:L/U:Amber`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

Path Traversal and Missing Authorization in cloud-storage source in Google Cloud MCP Toolbox for Databases (googleapis/mcp-toolbox) versions 1.2.0 through 1.4.0 allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exfiltrate host files to external Google Cloud Storage buckets and overwrite arbitrary local files via crafted tool invocation parameters.

**solutions:** Upgrade googleapis/mcp-toolbox to version 1.5.0 or later.

Configure the security boundaries introduced in v1.5.0 by setting allowedLocalRoots to restrict host file system interactions strictly to designated, isolated directories set allowedBuckets to ensure the tool only reads from and writes to explicit, authorized Google Cloud Storage buckets.

Follow the Principle of Least Privilege by running the Toolbox service under an unprivileged OS user account and restricting associated Google Cloud IAM permissions.

Affected:
- Google Cloud / MCP Toolbox for Databases (googleapis/mcp-toolbox): affected 1.2.0 <1.5.0 (custom)

Credits: He Wei (gikaku)

References:
- https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox/pull/3454

### CVE-2026-95702 — Code Execution in Host Sentry Process via Double Free in gVisor VFS MemoryFile
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-10-09 | Updated: 2026-10-15 | Max CVSS: 8.5
- CWE: CWE-416 CWE-416 Use After Free; CWE-415 CWE-415 Double Free
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.5 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Use-after-free vulnerability in VFS in Google gVisor prior to release 20260831.0 on all platforms allows a local attacker with standard container privileges to achieve code execution in the host sentry process by double-freeing the backing MemoryFile from an in-sandbox overlay filesystem. The sentry process remains confined by host-level Linux seccomp and namespace boundaries.

Affected:
- Google / gVisor: affected 0 <20260831.0 (semver)

Credits: Mikhail Sosonkin from OpenAI

References:
- https://github.com/google/gvisor/commit/90bc4fc36fe442257a06ba15df00371561c183ed

### CVE-2026-96812 — Host Root Sandbox Escape in gVisor via Character Device Passthrough and CUSE
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-09-25 | Updated: 2026-09-25 | Max CVSS: 8.8
- CWE: CWE-668 CWE-668 Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere; CWE-269 CWE-269 Improper Privilege Management
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.8 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:P/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:H/SI:H/SA:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Improper Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere in the host file helper (gofer) in Google gVisor prior to commit 573a9e73cf844f on Linux platforms with CUSE enabled allows a local attacker with container image deployment privileges to achieve root code execution on the host system. By including a /dev/cuse character device node in a container image, opening the device passes through to the host, allowing the sandboxed attacker to register a host device and exploit CUSE unrestricted ioctl handling to overwrite root udev helper memory.

Affected:
- Google / gVisor: affected 0 <573a9e73cf844f (git)

Credits: Anthropic (using Claude)

References:
- https://github.com/google/gvisor/commit/573a9e73cf844f

### CVE-2026-102242 — Path Traversal via Symlink Following in allowedLocalRoots in MCP Toolbox for Databases
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-09-29 | Updated: 2026-09-29 | Max CVSS: 8.6
- CWE: CWE-59 CWE-59 Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following'); CWE-22 CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.6 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Improper link resolution (CWE-59 / CWE-22) in the allowedLocalRoots path validation in Google MCP Toolbox for Databases versions 1.2.0 through 1.9.0 allows a remote authenticated attacker with tool execution permissions to bypass directory boundary restrictions via symbolic links. Because path validation checks directories lexically without resolving symbolic links first, an attacker can access or overwrite arbitrary local files located outside the permitted root directories.

Affected:
- Google / MCP Toolbox for Databases: affected 1.2.0 <=1.9.0 (semver)

Credits: Emmanuel David Karganilla

References:
- https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox/pull/3810

### CVE-2026-102503 — Missing Authentication on /libp2p-http Ingress in Google OSS Agent Mesh (SAM)
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-10-19 | Updated: 2026-10-19 | Max CVSS: 9.3
- CWE: CWE-306 CWE-306 Missing Authentication for Critical Function; CWE-862 CWE-862 Missing Authorization
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.3 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

Missing Authentication for Critical Function (CWE-306) and Missing Authorization (CWE-862) in the /libp2p-http ingress server (StartIngressServer in cmd/sam-node/node.go) in Google OSS Agent Mesh (SAM) versions 0.1.0-alpha.1 through 0.1.0-alpha.2 allow an unauthenticated remote libp2p peer to bypass Biscuit capability policy enforcement and invoke arbitrary registered backend services (including command/stdio-backed MCP servers, A2A, and inference endpoints). While the MCP protocol stream handler enforces WithBiscuitAuth and Authorize checks, the parallel /libp2p-http ingress routes requests directly to backend service handlers without verifying a Biscuit token or mesh enrollment. Users should upgrade to version 0.1.0-alpha.3 or later.

Affected:
- Google / SAM: affected 0.1.0-alpha.1 <0.1.0-alpha.3 (semver)

Credits: Yanchon918s

### CVE-2026-102554 — Denial of Service via Eager Array Allocation During Deserialization in Guava
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-10-09 | Updated: 2026-10-09 | Max CVSS: 8.2
- CWE: CWE-770 CWE-770 Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling; CWE-502 CWE-502 Deserialization of Untrusted Data

- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

Allocation of resources without limits or throttling (CWE-770) during Java object deserialization in Google Guava versions 4.0 through 33.7.1 allows an attacker to cause a Denial of Service via OutOfMemoryError. When deserializing CompactHashMap, CompactHashSet, or MapMakerInternalMap instances, Guava eagerly allocates an array based on a caller-specified size parameter without throttling, permitting memory exhaustion from crafted serialization streams.

### CVE-2026-103090 — Unauthenticated Biscuit Credential Disclosure via GET /enroll/status in Google OSS Agent Mesh (SAM)
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-10-21 | Updated: 2026-10-30 | Max CVSS: 8.8
- CWE: CWE-306 CWE-306 Missing Authentication for Critical Function; CWE-522 CWE-522 Insufficiently Protected Credentials
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.8 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:L/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Missing Authentication for Critical Function (CWE-306) and Insufficiently Protected Credentials (CWE-522) in the control plane enrollment status handler (HandleEnrollStatus at GET /enroll/status in internal/controlplane/server.go) in Google OSS Agent Mesh (SAM) versions 0.1.0-alpha.1 through 0.1.0-alpha.8 allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to retrieve an approved bootstrap-enrolled peer's signed Biscuit identity token by supplying a peer_id obtainable from the unauthenticated GET /info endpoint. A related flaw in POST /enroll allowed any bootstrap-token holder to re-fetch another peer's credential. An attacker can replay the disclosed Biscuit token as a bearer credential on /policies to read mesh authorization policies and on /routers/lease to overwrite advertised router multiaddrs. Users should upgrade to version 0.1.0-alpha.9 or later, which requires cryptographic proof of possession of the enrollment private key on credential-releasing endpoints, enforces rate limiting, and validates router lease addresses.

Affected:
- Google / SAM: affected 0.1.0-alpha.1 <0.1.0-alpha.9 (semver)

Credits: makino-yuto

References:
- https://github.com/google/sam/security/advisories/GHSA-hp3x-79wr-rx66 [vendor-advisory]
- https://github.com/google/sam/releases/tag/v0.1.0-alpha.9 [release-notes]
- https://github.com/google/agentmesh/security/advisories/GHSA-hp3x-79wr-rx66 [exploit]

### CVE-2026-103091 — Insecure Default Policy and Unrestricted OIDC Enrollment in Google OSS Agent Mesh (SAM)
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-10-19 | Updated: 2026-10-19 | Max CVSS: 9.3
- CWE: CWE-862 CWE-862 Missing Authorization; CWE-1188 CWE-1188 Initialization of a Resource with an Insecure Default; CWE-306 CWE-306 Missing Authentication for Critical Function; CWE-863 CWE-863 Incorrect Authorization; CWE-200 CWE-200 Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.3 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Missing Authorization (CWE-862) and Initialization of a Resource with an Insecure Default (CWE-1188) in the MCP proxy (HandleStreamPassThrough in mcp_service.go) and OIDC registration flow (GET /info and POST /register in internal/controlplane/server.go) in Google OSS Agent Mesh (SAM) versions 0.1.0-alpha.1 through 0.1.0-alpha.8 allow a remote attacker to self-enroll into the mesh and invoke arbitrary tools across all connected MCP backend nodes. Because GET /info publicly discloses OIDC configuration, POST /register auto-enrolls any valid OIDC token holder without claim filtering or ban checks, and the default policy binds sam:system:authenticated to wildcard services and targets, an attacker can obtain a mesh credential with full read, write, and execution access on backend services. Users should upgrade to version 0.1.0-alpha.9 or later, which enforces a fail-closed default policy, explicit policy-binding requirements on enrollment, and ban checks.

Affected:
- Google / SAM: affected 0.1.0-alpha.1 <0.1.0-alpha.9 (semver)

Credits: Eli Ainhorn (Noma Security)

References:
- https://github.com/google/sam/security/advisories/GHSA-cgmg-9xf6-rrgw [vendor-advisory]
- https://github.com/google/sam/releases/tag/v0.1.0-alpha.9 [release-notes]
- https://github.com/google/agentmesh/security/advisories/GHSA-cgmg-9xf6-rrgw [exploit]

### CVE-2026-105222 — alexpechkarev/google-maps through 12.16 Disabled TLS Certificate Verification via ssl_verify_peer
- Assigner: VulnCheck | Published: 2026-10-04 | Updated: 2026-10-27 | Max CVSS: 9.1
- CWE: CWE-295 Improper Certificate Validation
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.1 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.4 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

The alexpechkarev/google-maps Laravel package through 12.16 disables TLS certificate verification by default because the bundled config sets ssl_verify_peer to FALSE, which is passed to CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER. On-path attackers can present any certificate to intercept Google Maps web-service requests, steal the API key from the query string, and tamper with responses.

Affected:
- alexpechkarev / google-maps: affected 1.0.3 <=12.16 (custom)

Credits: Siyang Wu

References:
- https://github.com/alexpechkarev/google-maps/issues/123 [issue-tracking]

### CVE-2026-107858 — Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking and Permissive CORS in Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) for Java Development Server
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-10-23 | Updated: 2026-11-02 | Max CVSS: 7.2
- CWE: CWE-1385 CWE-1385 Missing Origin Validation in WebSockets; CWE-942 CWE-942 Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains; CWE-306 CWE-306 Missing Authentication for Critical Function
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 7.2 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:P/VC:H/VI:L/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

Missing Origin Validation in WebSockets (CWE-1385) and Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains (CWE-942) in the development web server (ADK Web) in Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) for Java (com.google.adk:google-adk-dev versions 0.1.0 before 1.13.0 and com.google.adk:google-adk-maven-plugin versions 0.3.0 before 1.13.0) allow a remote attacker to control a locally running agent and read its data via a malicious web page visited by a developer while the server is running. The /run_live WebSocket endpoint accepts connections from any origin by default (hardcoded via setAllowedOrigins("*") in versions 0.1.0 through 1.5.0, and defaulting to * via adk.web.cors.origins in versions 1.6.0 through 1.12.0), and since version 0.4.0 the REST API returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * by default. Because the server has no authentication and requests originate from the developer's browser (so binding to localhost does not prevent exploitation), a cross-origin page can send messages to the agent (triggering registered tools), stream agent responses, and list, read, create, or delete sessions and artifacts. In versions 1.6.0 through 1.12.0, users can mitigate the issue by setting the adk.web.cors.origins property to an explicit allowlist of trusted origins (such as http://localhost:8000). The vulnerability is fixed in version 1.13.0, which enforces a same-origin default for CORS and the /run_live WebSocket endpoint, and rejects DNS-rebinding requests over loopback.

**workarounds:** For versions 1.6.0 through 1.12.0, configure the adk.web.cors.origins property to an explicit allowlist of trusted origins (for example, http://localhost:8000) to restrict both the REST API and the /run_live WebSocket endpoint.

**solutions:** Upgrade Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) for Java to version 1.13.0 or later.

Affected:
- Google / Agent Development Kit (ADK) for Java: affected 0.1.0 <1.13.0 (semver)
- Google / Agent Development Kit (ADK) for Java: affected 0.3.0 <1.13.0 (semver)

Credits: George Chen (@geo-chen); Gouri Sankar A (@g0w6y)

- https://github.com/google/adk-java/issues/1257 [issue-tracking,exploit]
- https://github.com/google/adk-java/releases/tag/v1.13.0 [release-notes]
- https://github.com/google/adk-java/commit/5667d382ab5078a0d6e8f7184713a6bab767e004 [patch]
- https://github.com/google/adk-java/commit/1ae5078072e13e101318e32833f1db323ef084e1 [patch]
- https://github.com/google/adk-java/pull/1222 [mitigation,patch]

### CVE-2026-111497 — Out-of-Bounds Write in Google Brotli Decoder
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-10-22 | Updated: 2026-11-10 | Max CVSS: 9.2
- CWE: CWE-787 CWE-787 Out-of-bounds Write; CWE-252 CWE-252 Unchecked Return Value
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.2 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=active, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- **CISA KEV**: added 2026-10-27, ransomware=Unknown — Google Brotli Unchecked Return Value Vulnerability

A buffer overflow vulnerability in the Brotli decoder (c/dec/decode.c) in Google Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 on all platforms allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service, or potentially execute arbitrary code using a crafted Brotli-compressed stream.





Users need to update any Brotli libraries or binaries between 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 to the latest available version: 1.0.10 or 1.1.1 or 1.2.1.

**solutions:** Update any Brotli libraries or binaries between 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 to the latest available version: 1.0.10 or 1.1.1 or 1.2.1.

Affected:
- Google / Brotli: affected 1.0.3 <1.0.10 (semver); affected 1.1.0 <1.1.1 (semver); affected 1.2.0 <1.2.1 (semver)
- Siemens / Calibre: unaffected 0 <* (custom)
- Siemens / Calibre ICE: unaffected 0 <* (custom)
- Siemens / Capital: unaffected 0 <* (custom)
- Siemens / Cloud Connector Configurator: affected 0 <V1.24.3 (custom)
- Siemens / Common Configurator (CC on IEM): affected 0 <* (custom)
- Siemens / Common Configurator on Device (CC on Edge): affected 0 <* (custom)
- Siemens / COMOS Walkinside: affected 0 <* (custom)
- Siemens / Data Flow Monitoring: affected 0 <V3.0.18 (custom)
- Siemens / Databus Configurator: affected 0 <V4.0.1 (custom)
- Siemens / DataXess Configurator: affected 0 <V1.5.7 (custom)
- Siemens / Designcenter X Essentials: unaffected 0 <* (custom)
- Siemens / Desigo CC family V8: affected 0 <* (custom)
- Siemens / Desigo CC family V9: affected 0 <* (custom)
- Siemens / Edge OPC UA Server Configurator: affected 0 <V2.3.10 (custom)

### CVE-2026-115522 — Cross-Application Artifact Namespace Isolation in Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) for Python
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2026-10-28 | Updated: 2026-11-05 | Max CVSS: 5.3
- CWE: CWE-668 CWE-668 Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 5.3 MEDIUM `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:L/VI:L/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere (CWE-668) in FileArtifactService in Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) for Python (google-adk) versions 1.19.0 before 1.39.1 and 2.0.0a1 before 2.7.0 allows a caller in one application to list, read, overwrite, or delete artifacts belonging to another application when both applications share a FileArtifactService root directory and use the same user_id (and session_id for session-scoped artifacts). FileArtifactService accepted app_name across its public API methods but omitted app_name when constructing on-disk paths (root/users/{user_id}/... instead of root/apps/{app_name}/users/{user_id}/...). Version 2.6.0 scoped writes by app_name but retained a legacy root/users/{user_id} fallback for reads and deletes; version 2.7.0 and the 1.x backport in version 1.39.1 removed the fallback and enforce full per-app path scoping.

**solutions:** Upgrade Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) for Python (google-adk) to version 1.39.1 (for 1.x installations) or version 2.7.0 (for 2.x installations) or later.

Affected:
- Google / Agent Development Kit (ADK) for Python: affected 1.19.0 <1.39.1 (semver); affected 2.0.0a1 <2.7.0 (semver)

Credits: @Nant361

- https://github.com/google/adk-python/commit/c27d8688ed9ea619587ad96cbfd641c34dd7340c [patch]
- https://github.com/google/adk-python/commit/0ae2bffdd2628af6c8643bc4fd40c2f49f0c6bd4 [patch]
